title: Simplify by hand
starter:
%x = param 0 dtype=i32
%a = add 3 %x
%z = mul %x 0
%b = add %a %z
%out = add %b 5
hints: Which parts of the graph are pure constants, and which parts are an identity you can drop?
On i32, `x * 0` is always 0, and adding 0 changes nothing. That leaves `(3 + x) + 5`.
i32 addition is a ring mod 2^32, so you can regroup `(3 + x) + 5` as `x + (3 + 5)` even when it wraps at `INT_MAX`.

answer.explain: On i32, `mul x 0` is exactly 0 and `add _ 0` is the identity. Reassociation is safe because wraparound arithmetic is still associative, so the whole graph folds to `add %x 8`. That is one op, and it wraps the same way the original does at `INT_MAX`.
